question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Catch someone's eye
option_1: To irritate or annoy someone intentionally
option_2: To physically capture someone's gaze and hold it, making them unable to look away
option_3: To attract someone's attention or to be noticed by them
option_4: To surprise someone with unexpected behaviour
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To attract someone's attention or to be noticed by them.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "catch someone's eye" means to attract someone's attention or to be noticed by them. (किसी का ध्यान आकर्षित करना)

◦ Example: The bright red dress in the window caught my eye.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are literal misreadings; the idiom is not about annoying, forcibly holding a gaze, or surprising someone.

NOTE

• Related idioms with "eye": "keep an eye on" (watch), "see eye to eye" (agree), "turn a blind eye" (ignore), "in the public eye" (well known).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Revaeled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Revaeled" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Revealed", meaning made known or disclosed something previously secret. (प्रकट किया / उजागर किया)

◦ Example: The investigation revealed the truth.

• Spelling key: RE + VEAL + ED (the vowels are "ea", not "ae").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Search", "Multiple" and "Creative" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related forms: reveal (verb), revelation (noun), revealing (adjective). Watch the "ea" order in words like reveal, conceal, appeal and reveal.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Much of the beauty and glory of life have disappeared.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. have disappeared.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Much" is an uncountable (singular) quantifier, so it takes a singular verb. Hence "much of the beauty ... has disappeared", not "have disappeared".

◦ Correct: Much of the beauty and glory of life has disappeared.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Much of the", "beauty and glory" and "of life" are all correct; the subject "Much of the beauty and glory" is treated as singular.

NOTE

• Rule: "Much / a great deal of / a large amount of + uncountable noun" takes a singular verb. Compare with "Many + plural noun", which takes a plural verb.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

Mohit have appreciated Riya for her hard work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. has appreciated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mohit" is a third person singular subject, so in the present perfect tense it takes "has + past participle" → "Mohit has appreciated Riya for her hard work."

◦ Example: She has finished her work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "had appreciating" mixes past perfect auxiliary with the -ing form — wrong.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "have appreciated" does not agree with the singular "Mohit".

• Option 3 "have appreciates" is doubly wrong (plural auxiliary + -s verb).

NOTE

• Present perfect: has (singular) / have (plural) + past participle (V3). Mohit → has appreciated.

question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

Among the three little cats, the first was __________ and the second was smaller.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. small.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contrasts the first cat with the second ("the second was smaller"), so the first is described in the positive degree — "small". Using a comparative/superlative here would be grammatically wrong.

◦ Correct: The first was small and the second was smaller.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more small" and Option 3 "most small" are wrong; "small" forms its degrees as small – smaller – smallest.

• Option 4 "most smallest" is a double superlative, which is always incorrect.

NOTE

• Degrees of "small": small (positive) – smaller (comparative) – smallest (superlative). Never use "more/most" with the -er/-est forms.

question:
Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options.

While threatening the integrity of Universal values, the campaign to spread democracy will not suceed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Succeed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Succeed", meaning to achieve a desired aim or result. (सफल होना)

◦ Example: Hard work will help you succeed.

• Spelling key: SUC + CEED — double "c" and "-cceed" ending.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 3 and 4 ("Suucced", "Sucseed", "Succsed") are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Only three English verbs end in "-cceed": succeed, proceed, exceed end differently — note "succeed/proceed/exceed" vs the "-cede" family (precede, recede, concede).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'zest' in the given sentence.

The peppy and energetic music of the DJ was able to remove the passivity and dullness present in the party.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. dullness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Zest" means great enthusiasm, energy and excitement. (उत्साह / जोश)

• Its antonym is "dullness" — a lack of energy, liveliness or interest.

◦ Example: The party lost its zest and sank into dullness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 3 "energetic" and 4 "peppy" are synonyms of zest (full of energy).

• Option 1 "remove" is a verb, unrelated to the meaning of zest.

NOTE

• Synonyms of zest: enthusiasm, gusto, relish, zeal. Antonyms: dullness, apathy, indifference, listlessness.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

Sonali uses a soft mattress to sleep.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. hard.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Soft" means easy to press, yielding or not firm. Its antonym is "hard", meaning firm, solid and not easily pressed. (कठोर / सख्त)

◦ Example: The old wooden bench was very hard to sit on.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "flabby", Option 2 "cushiony" and Option 4 "spongy" are all synonyms of soft, not antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of soft: tender, cushiony, spongy, plush. Antonyms: hard, firm, rigid, stiff.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Baker's Dozen
option_2: One unit extra with one dozen
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. One unit extra with one dozen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "baker's dozen" means thirteen — one unit extra with the usual dozen (12). (एक दर्जन के साथ एक अतिरिक्त = तेरह)

◦ Example: The shop gave us a baker's dozen — thirteen buns for the price of twelve.

• Historically, bakers added an extra loaf to avoid penalties for selling underweight bread.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 4 is close but too general; the idiom specifically means thirteen, not just "something extra".

NOTE

• "Baker's dozen" = 13. The idiom arose in medieval England, where laws punished bakers for short measures, so they gave a 13th item for safety.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Despite facing numerous challenges, the team successfully __________ the project ahead of schedule.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. completed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes a completed past action performed by the team, so the simple past active verb "completed" is correct — "the team successfully completed the project ahead of schedule."

◦ Example: They completed the assignment on time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "had completed" (past perfect) needs an earlier reference point, absent here.

• Option 2 "has been completed" is passive and does not fit the active subject "the team".

• Option 4 "will be completed" is future/passive, contradicting the completed sense.

NOTE

• Use the simple past for a finished action at a definite time in the past — here, completing the project ahead of schedule.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He is the friendly man in the group.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. friendliest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" before the adjective and the phrase "in the group" indicate a comparison among many, requiring the superlative degree — "the friendliest man in the group".

◦ Two-syllable adjectives ending in "-y" form the superlative with "-iest": friendly → friendliest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "most friendly" is a double/alternative superlative; with "-y" adjectives the "-iest" form is preferred (friendliest).

• Options 2 "friendlier" and 3 "more friendly" are comparative forms, used with "than", not "the ... in the group".

NOTE

• Degrees: friendly – friendlier – friendliest. The article "the" + "in the group" signals the superlative.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

This is one of best movies I have ever seen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. one of best.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "one of the + superlative + plural noun" requires the definite article "the". So "one of best" must be "one of the best".

◦ Correct: This is one of the best movies I have ever seen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "This is", "movies" and "I have ever seen" are all correct.

NOTE

• Fixed pattern: "one of the + superlative adjective + plural noun + (that) + subject + has/have ever + past participle" — e.g., one of the finest books I have ever read.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Stories are how we make __________ of our lives and of the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sense.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression "make sense of" means to understand or find meaning in something. Hence "how we make sense of our lives and of the world." (समझ बनाना / अर्थ निकालना)

◦ Example: I couldn't make sense of his confusing directions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "sensitivity" is a noun but does not fit the idiom "make ___ of".

• Options 3 "innate" and 4 "sagacious" are adjectives and grammatically wrong here.

NOTE

• Common collocations with "sense": make sense of, a sense of humour, common sense, sixth sense, come to one's senses.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling error of the underlined word.

The historic cathedrel stood as a symbol of faith and architectural marvel, drawing visitors from around the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. cathedral.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "cathedral" — the principal church of a diocese, containing the bishop's throne. (गिरजाघर / कैथेड्रल)

◦ Example: The cathedral is famous for its stained-glass windows.

• Spelling key: CA + THE + DRAL (ends in "-dral").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 ("cathidrel", "cathedril", "cathidral") are all misspellings.

NOTE

• The word comes from "cathedra" (the bishop's seat). Related architecture words: basilica, chapel, abbey, monastery.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Fondness
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Liking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fondness" means a strong liking or affection for someone or something. (लगाव / स्नेह)

◦ Example: She has a great fondness for classical music.

• Its closest synonym is "liking".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Mistake" and Option 3 "Brilliance" are unrelated.

• Option 4 "Dislike" is the antonym of fondness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fondness: affection, attachment, liking, tenderness. Antonyms: dislike, aversion, hatred.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She asked if he could recount a moment when he felt completely serene.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. turbulent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Serene" means calm, peaceful and untroubled. Its antonym is "turbulent", meaning full of disturbance, agitation or unrest. (अशांत / उथल-पुथल भरा)

◦ Example: The sea was calm at dawn but grew turbulent by noon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "pacific" (peaceful) is a synonym of serene.

• Option 3 "hilarious" (very funny) and Option 4 "derogatory" (insulting) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of serene: calm, tranquil, placid, peaceful. Antonyms: turbulent, agitated, stormy, troubled.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Departing or having departed from a country to settle elsewhere
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Emigrant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "emigrant" is a person who leaves their own country to settle permanently in another. (उत्प्रवासी — देश छोड़कर जाने वाला)

◦ Example: Many emigrants left Europe for America in the 19th century.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Immigrant" is the opposite direction — one who comes into a country to settle.

• Option 2 "Excommunicate" means to formally exclude someone from a religious community.

• Option 4 "Native" means a person born in a particular place.

NOTE

• Memory tip: Emigrant Exits a country; Immigrant comes Into a country. Both may describe the same person from different viewpoints.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Although experts are worried / that retail inflation is rising / at a steep rate, / the crisis will soon blow away.
option_3: the crisis will soon blow away
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the crisis will soon blow away.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct idiom is "blow over", meaning (of a problem or crisis) to pass off or subside without serious consequences, not "blow away".

◦ Correct: ... the crisis will soon blow over.

• "Blow away" means to remove by wind or to impress greatly — wrong in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Although experts are worried", "that retail inflation is rising" and "at a steep rate" are all correct.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "blow": blow over (pass/subside), blow up (explode/get angry), blow away (impress/remove by wind), blow out (extinguish).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

In the absence of her parents, the little girl felt __________ (lonely).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. alone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lonely" means sad from being without companionship; isolated. Its closest synonym here is "alone", conveying being by oneself. (अकेला)

◦ Example: With everyone away, she felt completely alone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "collectively" (together) and Option 2 "crowded" are opposite in sense.

• Option 4 "sociable" (fond of company) is an antonym of lonely.

NOTE

• Synonyms of lonely: alone, solitary, forlorn, isolated, friendless. Antonyms: sociable, accompanied, crowded.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A room for cleaning and storing dishes and cooking utensils and for doing messy kitchen work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Scullery.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "scullery" is a small room next to the kitchen used for washing dishes, storing utensils and doing rough, messy kitchen work. (रसोई से लगा भंडार-कक्ष)

◦ Example: The maid washed the pots in the scullery.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Dormitory" — a large bedroom for several people.

• Option 3 "Sanatorium" — an establishment for the treatment/recovery of the sick.

• Option 4 "Overlay" — a covering layer (not a room).

NOTE

• Related "room" words: pantry (food storage), larder (cool food store), cellar (underground store), vestibule (entrance hall).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The (1)__________ life in Kashmir was drawing to its end after three (2)__________ months. Miss Joan was leaving a week earlier than Mrs. Rhodes, and about two days before she left, I took her alone to the hotel for dinner. We walked to the hotel in (3)__________ silence, a silence so heavy that I could (4)__________ breathe. The hotel seemed to be far away and yet not far (5)__________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. romantic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The context of a memorable stay in beautiful Kashmir with a companion calls for the adjective "romantic" — meaning charming, idealised and full of feeling. "The romantic life in Kashmir was drawing to its end." (रोमांटिक / भावपूर्ण)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "tonetic" (relating to tones/phonetics), Option 3 "biquadratic" (a maths term) and Option 4 "mucolytic" (a medical term) make no sense in this literary context.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, first fix the meaning required by the context, then check that the word's part of speech fits the blank.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The (1)__________ life in Kashmir was drawing to its end after three (2)__________ months. Miss Joan was leaving a week earlier than Mrs. Rhodes, and about two days before she left, I took her alone to the hotel for dinner. We walked to the hotel in (3)__________ silence, a silence so heavy that I could (4)__________ breathe. The hotel seemed to be far away and yet not far (5)__________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. glorious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Glorious" means wonderful, delightful and marked by beauty or splendour. It fits "three glorious months" spent in the scenic beauty of Kashmir. (शानदार / भव्य)

◦ Example: We had a glorious holiday in the hills.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "anonymous" (of unknown name), Option 2 "analogous" (comparable) and Option 3 "jealous" (envious) do not suit a description of enjoyable months.

NOTE

• Synonyms of glorious: splendid, magnificent, wonderful, delightful. All the distractors end in "-ous" but differ sharply in meaning.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The (1)__________ life in Kashmir was drawing to its end after three (2)__________ months. Miss Joan was leaving a week earlier than Mrs. Rhodes, and about two days before she left, I took her alone to the hotel for dinner. We walked to the hotel in (3)__________ silence, a silence so heavy that I could (4)__________ breathe. The hotel seemed to be far away and yet not far (5)__________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. perfect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Perfect" here means complete and absolute — "we walked to the hotel in perfect silence", i.e. total, unbroken silence, which the next clause confirms ("a silence so heavy"). (पूर्ण / संपूर्ण)

◦ Example: The class listened in perfect silence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "direct", Option 3 "select" and Option 4 "slack" do not collocate meaningfully with "silence".

NOTE

• Collocation: "in perfect silence", "in complete silence", "in dead silence" — all mean total quiet.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The (1)__________ life in Kashmir was drawing to its end after three (2)__________ months. Miss Joan was leaving a week earlier than Mrs. Rhodes, and about two days before she left, I took her alone to the hotel for dinner. We walked to the hotel in (3)__________ silence, a silence so heavy that I could (4)__________ breathe. The hotel seemed to be far away and yet not far (5)__________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. hardly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hardly" means scarcely / almost not at all. The phrase "a silence so heavy that I could hardly breathe" conveys that the silence was so oppressive the narrator could barely breathe. (मुश्किल से)

◦ Example: It was so cold that I could hardly move my fingers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "loudly", Option 3 "gladly" and Option 4 "gradually" do not fit the sense of an oppressive, breath-stifling silence.

NOTE

• "Hardly", "scarcely" and "barely" are negative adverbs meaning "almost not". They should not be used with another negative (no "couldn't hardly").

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The (1)__________ life in Kashmir was drawing to its end after three (2)__________ months. Miss Joan was leaving a week earlier than Mrs. Rhodes, and about two days before she left, I took her alone to the hotel for dinner. We walked to the hotel in (3)__________ silence, a silence so heavy that I could (4)__________ breathe. The hotel seemed to be far away and yet not far (5)__________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. enough.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enough" completes the idea "far away and yet not far enough" — meaning the hotel seemed distant, yet not distant enough (to delay the painful parting). (पर्याप्त)

◦ Example: The rope was long, but not long enough to reach.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "thorough" (complete), Option 2 "overweigh" (a verb) and Option 3 "clough" (a ravine) do not fit grammatically or in sense.

NOTE

• "Enough" follows the adjective/adverb it modifies: "far enough", "good enough", "old enough" — unlike "very", which precedes it.

question: The Republic Day parade is held every year at Kartavya Path, in which of the following cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Republic Day parade is held every year on 26 January at Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath) in New Delhi. (कर्तव्य पथ, नई दिल्ली)

• Republic Day commemorates the coming into force of the Constitution of India on 26 January 1950.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Rajpath" was renamed "Kartavya Path" in September 2022 as part of the Central Vista redevelopment.

• The parade proceeds from Rashtrapati Bhavan to the Red Fort, and a foreign Head of State is usually the chief guest.

NOTE

• 26 January was chosen because the Purna Swaraj (complete independence) resolution was celebrated on that date in 1930.

question: What is the term for the maximum population size that an environment can sustain indefinitely?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carrying capacity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Carrying capacity" is the maximum population size of a species that a given environment can support indefinitely, given the available food, habitat, water and other resources. (धारण क्षमता)

• It is usually denoted by the symbol "K" in population ecology.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ecological niche — the role and position a species occupies in its ecosystem.

• Pioneer species — the first organisms to colonise a barren area (e.g., lichens).

• Biotic potential — the maximum reproductive capacity of a population under ideal conditions.

NOTE

• When a population exceeds the carrying capacity, resource depletion leads to a decline, keeping the population near K in a logistic (S-shaped) growth curve.

question: According to Census 2011 of India, which Indian state has the highest urban population percentage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to Census 2011, Goa had the highest percentage of urban population among Indian states, with about 62.2% of its population living in urban areas. (गोवा — सर्वाधिक शहरी जनसंख्या प्रतिशत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mizoram (about 52%) and Tamil Nadu (about 48%) are among the other highly urbanised states.

• Among Union Territories, Delhi and Chandigarh are almost entirely urban.

• Himachal Pradesh had the lowest urban share among states.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census of India; the overall urban population of India was about 31.16%.

question: In the Vedic period, education was begun with which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Upanayana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Vedic period, formal education began with the "Upanayana" ceremony — a sacred thread (Yajnopavita) initiation rite that marked a boy's entry into student life (Brahmacharya) under a guru. (उपनयन संस्कार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The four ashramas (stages of life) were Brahmacharya (student), Grihastha (householder), Vanaprastha (forest-dweller/retirement) and Sannyasa (renunciation).

• Education was largely oral, based on learning the Vedas by heart in the gurukul system.

NOTE

• Upanayana is one of the traditional sixteen samskaras (rites of passage) in Hindu tradition.

question: In which neighbouring country of India is the Haa Summer Festival celebrated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhutan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Haa Summer Festival" is celebrated in the Haa Valley of Bhutan. It showcases the traditional living culture, nomadic lifestyle, cuisine, and religious practices of the Bhutanese people. (हा समर फेस्टिवल — भूटान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bhutan, a landlocked Himalayan kingdom, is famous for measuring progress through "Gross National Happiness (GNH)".

• Its capital is Thimphu, and its currency is the Ngultrum.

NOTE

• Other Bhutanese festivals: Paro Tshechu and Thimphu Tshechu, featuring masked (Cham) dances.

question: Who among the following is appointed as the chairman of the 16th Finance Commission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arvind Panagariya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr Arvind Panagariya, an eminent economist and former Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog, was appointed the Chairman of the 16th Finance Commission (constituted in 2023). (16वाँ वित्त आयोग — अरविंद पनगढ़िया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280, constituted every five years by the President.

• Its main task is to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and the states (vertical and horizontal devolution).

• The 15th Finance Commission was chaired by N. K. Singh.

NOTE

• The 16th Finance Commission's recommendations will cover the period 2026–2031.

question: The memoir of which of the following actors is titled 'Unfinished'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Priyanka Chopra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unfinished" is the memoir of the actor Priyanka Chopra Jonas, published in 2021. It recounts her journey from India to global stardom. (प्रियंका चोपड़ा की संस्मरण पुस्तक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Priyanka Chopra won Miss World 2000 and later became a leading Bollywood and Hollywood actor (e.g., the TV series *Quantico*).

• She has been a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador.

NOTE

• Other celebrity memoirs/autobiographies: *The Substance and the Shadow* (Dilip Kumar), *Khullam Khulla* (Rishi Kapoor), *An Unsuitable Boy* (Karan Johar).

question: On 16 February 2023, who was sworn in as the new Governor of Sikkim at Raj Bhawan, Gangtok?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lakshman Prasad Acharya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lakshman Prasad Acharya was sworn in as the Governor of Sikkim at Raj Bhawan, Gangtok, on 16 February 2023. (सिक्किम के राज्यपाल — लक्ष्मण प्रसाद आचार्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state (Articles 153–162), appointed by the President and holding office during the President's pleasure.

• Gangtok is the capital of Sikkim, which became the 22nd state of India in 1975.

NOTE

• Pawan Chamling (a long-serving former Chief Minister of Sikkim) and Ganga Prasad (a former Governor) are used here as distractors.

question: Which of the following Harappan cities was found without a citadel?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chanhudaro.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chanhudaro is the only major Harappan city found without a citadel (fortified upper town). It was primarily a craft and bead-making centre. (चन्हूदड़ो — बिना दुर्ग वाला नगर)

• It is located in Sindh (present-day Pakistan) and was excavated by N. G. Majumdar (1931).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Most Harappan cities (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Kalibangan, Lothal, Banawali) had a citadel to the west and a lower town to the east.

• Chanhudaro was famous for bead-making, seal-making and metal working.

NOTE

• Lothal (Gujarat) is known for its dockyard; Kalibangan (Rajasthan) for ploughed fields and fire altars.

question: What is the year of foundation of the Women's Indian Association (WIA)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1917.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Women's Indian Association (WIA) was founded in 1917 at Adyar, Madras (Chennai), by Annie Besant, Margaret Cousins, Dorothy Jinarajadasa and others. It worked for women's education, welfare and voting rights. (महिला भारतीय संघ — 1917)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The WIA was one of the earliest organisations to demand women's suffrage (right to vote) in India.

• 1917 was also the year of Annie Besant's presidency of the Congress (Calcutta session) and the launch of the Home Rule Movement's peak activity.

NOTE

• Other women's organisations: All India Women's Conference (AIWC), 1927 and the National Council of Women in India, 1925.

question: Which of the following Acts was the first intervention by the British government in the East India Company's territorial affairs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Regulating Act, 1773.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first intervention by the British Parliament in the affairs of the East India Company, marking the beginning of parliamentary control over Company administration in India. (रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट, 1773)

• It made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings being the first) and established a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Pitt's India Act, 1784 established dual control by setting up a Board of Control alongside the Court of Directors.

• The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly (except tea and trade with China).

NOTE

• The Regulating Act was the first step in the constitutional development of British rule; it had defects later corrected by the Amending Act of 1781 and Pitt's India Act.

question: In which of the following groups of States and Union Territories is 'slash and burn' agriculture known as 'Dipa'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Slash and burn" (shifting) agriculture is known as "Dipa" in Chhattisgarh and in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands. (झूम / स्थानांतरी कृषि — 'दीपा')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shifting cultivation has different local names across India:

◦ Jhum — North-East India; Podu — Andhra Pradesh/Odisha; Bewar/Dahiya — Madhya Pradesh; Kumari — Western Ghats; Penda — Chhattisgarh.

NOTE

• In slash-and-burn farming, forest patches are cleared and burnt, cultivated for a few years, then abandoned for the soil to regain fertility.

question: A person with a very low count of red blood cells is medically known to have _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anaemia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anaemia" is a condition marked by a low count of red blood cells (RBCs) or of haemoglobin, reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity and causing fatigue and pallor. (रक्ताल्पता / एनीमिया)

• The most common cause is iron deficiency.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jaundice — yellowing of skin/eyes due to excess bilirubin (a liver-related condition).

• Goitre — swelling of the thyroid gland, usually due to iodine deficiency.

• Scurvy — caused by Vitamin C deficiency, leading to bleeding gums.

NOTE

• Haemoglobin, an iron-containing pigment in RBCs, carries oxygen; deficiency of iron, Vitamin B12 or folic acid can cause anaemia.

question: To which position in the Mughal administration under Akbar does Diwan-i-Ala refer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Finance Minister.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Akbar's administration, the "Diwan-i-Ala" (also called Wazir/Diwan) was the head of the revenue and finance department — effectively the Finance Minister of the empire. (दीवान-ए-आला — वित्त मंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other key Mughal officials:

◦ Mir Bakshi — head of the military/intelligence department.

◦ Sadr-us-Sudur — in charge of religious and charitable matters.

◦ Qazi-ul-Quzat — the chief judicial officer.

• Akbar introduced the Mansabdari system and the Zabti/Dahsala land revenue system (with Raja Todar Mal).

NOTE

• Todar Mal, Akbar's revenue minister, is closely associated with the office of Diwan and land-revenue reforms.

question: With which Kathak gharana was Pandit Janki Prasad affiliated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Benaras.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Janki Prasad is regarded as the founder of the Benaras (Banaras) gharana of Kathak. This gharana is known for its natural, graceful movements and its distinctive use of tatkar (footwork). (बनारस घराना — कथक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The major Kathak gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur, Benaras and (later) Raigarh.

◦ Lucknow gharana — emphasis on grace and expression (abhinaya); founded by Ishwari Prasad, developed by Thakur Prasad and Binda Din Maharaj.

◦ Jaipur gharana — emphasis on speed, spins and intricate footwork.

NOTE

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, associated mainly with North India.

question: Mukhya Mantri Sikho Kamao Yojana was launched by which of these state governments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mukhyamantri Sikho Kamao Yojana" (Chief Minister Learn and Earn Scheme) was launched by the Madhya Pradesh government in 2023 to provide skill training with a stipend to educated unemployed youth. (मुख्यमंत्री सीखो-कमाओ योजना — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Under the scheme, youth receive on-the-job training in industries while earning a monthly stipend, combining learning with earning.

• Madhya Pradesh also runs the Ladli Behna Yojana for women's welfare.

NOTE

• Such skilling schemes align with the national Skill India Mission and aim to improve youth employability.

question: Sitara Devi was a classical dancer of India who used to perform __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sitara Devi (1920–2014) was a legendary exponent of the Kathak classical dance form. She was called the "Kathak Queen", and Rabindranath Tagore praised her as "Nritya Samragni" (Empress of Dance). (कथक — सितारा देवी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• She was awarded the Padma Shri (1973), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1969) and the Kalidas Samman; she declined the Padma Bharti/Padma Bhushan, feeling it was below her stature.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances: Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Sattriya (Assam), Odissi (Odisha), Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Manipuri (Manipur).

question: When did the Hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand make his Olympic debut?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1928, Amsterdam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Hockey Wizard" Major Dhyan Chand made his Olympic debut at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, where India won its first Olympic gold medal in hockey. (मेजर ध्यानचंद — 1928 एम्स्टर्डम ओलंपिक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dhyan Chand won three Olympic golds — 1928 (Amsterdam), 1932 (Los Angeles) and 1936 (Berlin).

• His birthday, 29 August, is celebrated as National Sports Day in India.

• India's highest sporting honour was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2021.

NOTE

• Dhyan Chand scored over 400 goals in his international career and was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1956.

question: Which dance guru of Kuchipudi dance got Padma Bhushan in 1998?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam, a legendary exponent and teacher of Kuchipudi, was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1998 for his contribution to the dance form. (गुरु वेम्पति चिन्ना सत्यम — कुचिपुड़ी)

• He founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai and choreographed numerous dance-dramas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh, traditionally a dance-drama performed by men, later opened to women.

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was a legend of Odissi, not Kuchipudi.

NOTE

• Kuchipudi is noted for the Tarangam, in which the dancer performs on the rim of a brass plate.

question: The space-filling model emphasises the relative size of each atom based on its _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is van der Waals radius.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "space-filling model" (also called a CPK model) represents atoms as spheres whose radii are proportional to the van der Waals radius of each atom, showing the relative sizes and the space occupied by a molecule. (वान डर वाल्स त्रिज्या)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The van der Waals radius is half the distance between the nuclei of two non-bonded atoms of the same element at their closest approach.

• A ball-and-stick model, by contrast, emphasises bonds and bond angles rather than atomic size.

NOTE

• Order of atomic radii (roughly): van der Waals radius > metallic/covalent radius; cations are smaller and anions larger than the parent atom.

question: Australia won the Men's T20 World Cup Cricket in 2021 defeating New Zealand by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8 wickets.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the final of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021 (held in the UAE & Oman), Australia defeated New Zealand by 8 wickets to win their first men's T20 World Cup title. (ऑस्ट्रेलिया — 8 विकेट से विजयी)

• Mitchell Marsh (77*) played a match-winning knock; David Warner was Player of the Tournament.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It was Australia's maiden men's T20 World Cup title.

• The final was played at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.

NOTE

• India hosted/co-hosted later editions; the 2024 T20 World Cup was won by India.

question: What is the primary objective of Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) in India?
option_1: To provide financial services to large corporations
option_2: To offer financial assistance and services to low-income individuals and entrepreneurs
solution_text:
The correct answer is To offer financial assistance and services to low-income individuals and entrepreneurs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The primary objective of Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) is to provide small-scale financial services — credit, savings, insurance — to low-income individuals, small entrepreneurs and the poor who lack access to formal banking. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थान)

• This promotes financial inclusion and self-employment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• MFIs typically extend collateral-free micro-loans, often through Self Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups (JLGs).

• They are regulated by the RBI (many are registered as NBFC-MFIs).

NOTE

• The SHG–Bank Linkage Programme (NABARD, 1992) and institutions inspired by the Grameen Bank (Bangladesh) are central to India's microfinance movement.

question: 'Doabs' are found in which physical feature of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Northern Plains.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Doab" is the fertile alluvial land lying between two converging rivers, found in the Northern Plains of India. The word comes from Persian "do" (two) + "ab" (water). (दोआब — उत्तरी मैदान)

◦ Example: The Ganga–Yamuna Doab is one of the most fertile and densely populated regions of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Northern Plains are formed by the alluvial deposits of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems.

• They are divided into Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar (old alluvium) and Khadar (new alluvium).

NOTE

• Doabs are agriculturally very productive due to the deposition of fresh alluvium and the availability of water for irrigation.

question: The Indian Constitution originally consisted of how many Articles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 395.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Constitution originally consisted of 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules when it was adopted in 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950. (मूल संविधान — 395 अनुच्छेद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At present, the Constitution has about 470 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules (after various amendments), though Articles are still numbered up to 395 (with additions like 21A, 300A etc.).

• The Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly, with Dr. B. R. Ambedkar as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

NOTE

• It is the lengthiest written constitution in the world; it took the Constituent Assembly about 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to complete.

question: Water from melting snow or rainfall or the spring drains downwards through an area of land and finally gets mixed into a large water body like river or ocean. This area of land is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Drainage Basin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "drainage basin" (or catchment area) is the area of land drained by a river and its tributaries, from which all the water (from rain, snowmelt or springs) flows into a common outlet such as a river or ocean. (अपवाह द्रोणी / जलग्रहण क्षेत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The boundary separating two drainage basins is called a water divide (watershed).

• A delta is a depositional landform at a river's mouth; an estuary is where a river's freshwater meets the sea's saltwater; a bay is a broad inlet of the sea.

NOTE

• Major drainage basins of India include those of the Ganga, Brahmaputra, Indus, Godavari and Krishna rivers.
